A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WAFT optical-flow study. Their text, equations, four figures, six tables, and Appendix A are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original WAFT benchmark, zero-shot generalization, memory-profiling, and ablation results, including sequence-level Sintel results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original WAFT experimental outcomes in Tables 1–6, including benchmark evaluations, ablations, and the appendix analysis.

M1.justification: The encoder adaptations, recurrent DPT update module, feature-space warping, Mixture-of-Laplace loss, and convex upsampling are unchanged in Sections 4–5.1.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same optical-flow coverage: Sintel, KITTI, and Spring evaluations, with the same training datasets and zero-shot scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical across Tables 1–6. Flowformer++ and CCMR+, newly named in the headline speed comparison, were already evaluated in v2.

E3.justification: Training schedules, splits, model configurations, metrics, ablation controls, and 540p/1080p settings are unchanged. Table 2 retains latency measurements on an RTX3090 with batch size 1 and 540p input.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 and Table 5 retain the same component, resolution, and iterative-versus-direct ablations. Figure 3's boundary comparison and Appendix A's Ambush 1 outlier analysis are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 6's parenthetical values remain clean-pass EPE rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All measurements and entries in Tables 1–6 are identical. v3 newly quantifies the speed comparison with Flowformer++ as 1.3×, expanding the earlier 'up to 4.1×' summary. This limited reporting addition matches the existing Table 2 latencies of 374 ms for Flowformer++ and 290 ms for WAFT-Twins-a2.

T1.justification: The cost-volume, partial-cost-volume, and warping definitions in Sections 3.1–3.3 are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction refine the efficiency claim from 'up to 4.1×' to '1.3–4.1×' against methods with competitive accuracy, explicitly naming Flowformer++ and CCMR+. The central warping-alone, accuracy, and generalization claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations involving transformer attention, high-resolution indexing, iterative refinement, and context-encoder redundancy are retained. The qualification concerning Sintel's Ambush 1 sequence is unchanged, including in Appendix A.

D1.justification: Architecture details, hyperparameters, training schedules, hardware disclosures, and the code/model-weights availability statement are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work discussion are identical. Additional citation occurrences beside the speed examples refer to already discussed methods and do not revise the research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 expands three speed-summary passages, corrects 'fundamental level' to 'fundamental low-level,' and adds the ICLR 2026 publication header. Section organization and the remaining prose are retained.

P2.justification: The publication header and expanded sentences produce modest text reflow and within-page table shifts. Figures 1–4, table structures, captions, and the appendix display remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Naming the speed comparators and explicitly quantifying the Flowformer++ comparison makes the prominent efficiency claim easier to check against Table 2. Together with the terminology correction, this provides a limited clarity improvement; the methods, experimental evidence, and appendix analysis remain unchanged.
